definitions.gloss: pretending to be asleep; playing possum
definitions.explanation: Often used humorously or with mild criticism.

examples.japanese: タヌキ{寝入|ねい}りしてるでしょ。
examples.english: You're just pretending to be asleep, aren't you?

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧タヌキ{寝入|ねい}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{下手|へた}→下手：00703_heta⟧だ。
examples.english: Children are bad at pretending to be asleep.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦テレビ→テレビ：01536_terebi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧タヌキ{寝入|ねい}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いていなかった→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: My father was pretending to sleep in front of the TV and wasn't listening to the conversation.

notes:
Literally "tanuki sleep," from the folk belief that tanuki (⟦{狸|たぬき}→狸：04341_tanuki⟧, raccoon dogs) play dead to deceive people. Also written as ⟦{狸|たぬき}→狸：04341_tanuki⟧{寝入|ねい}り. The expression captures the idea of feigning sleep to avoid a situation or responsibility.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- タヌキ{寝入|ねい}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to pretend to be asleep
- タヌキ{寝入|ねい}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}め{込|こ}む→決め込む：13343_kimekomu⟧: to stubbornly pretend to be asleep

CULTURAL NOTE:
Tanuki are prominent in Japanese folklore as tricksters and shape-shifters. Many Japanese idioms reference their supposed cunning, such as {狸|たぬき}{親父|おやじ} (sly old man). The English equivalent "playing possum" draws on a similar animal-based metaphor.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{寝|ね}た→寝る：00470_neru⟧ふり: pretending to sleep (more neutral, no cultural connotation)
- ⟦{知|し}らん→知る：00458_shiru⟧ぷり: pretending not to know (different type of pretense)
